title: Where Should the Evaluation Budget Go in LLM-Driven Agent Scaffold Evolution?
abstract: arXiv:2610.37276v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language model (LLM)-driven agent scaffold evolution improves agent workflows through iterative candidate generation and evaluation. Evaluation both guides subsequent search and determines the final scaffold, but evaluating every candidate on the full task set incurs substantial execution costs. We investigate how evaluation budgets can be allocated across these two roles. Our experiments show that sparse feedback can sustain productive evolution, while additional targeted evaluation improves final selection. Replay analyses further show that shared informative items and a common scoring reference support comparisons among closely matched candidates. Motivated by these findings, we propose \method, an evaluation allocation framework that combines sparse search-time feedback with targeted final confirmation. A short fully evaluated warm-up establishes a shared informative core and calibrates a response model whose item parameters

translated_title: 在LLM驱动的智能体脚手架演化中，评估预算应该花在哪里？
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）驱动的智能体脚手架演化通过迭代式的候选生成与评估来改进智能体工作流程。评估既指导后续搜索，也决定最终的脚手架，但在完整任务集上评估每个候选会产生巨大的执行成本。我们研究了评估预算应如何在这两个角色之间进行分配。我们的实验表明，稀疏反馈能够维持富有成效的演化，而额外的针对性评估则可改善最终选择。重放分析进一步表明，共享的信息性任务项和共同的评分参考支持在表现相近的候选之间进行比较。基于这些发现，我们提出了\method，一个将稀疏的搜索时反馈与针对性的最终确认相结合的评估分配框架。一段简短的、经过完整评估的预热阶段建立了共享的信息核心，并校准了一个响应模型，其项目参数（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了一种评估预算分配框架，证明稀疏反馈足以维持演化搜索，而将额外预算用于针对性的最终确认环节，能更有效地选出最优的智能体脚手架。
